text:
alex: Quick q — we're proposing 365d retention for SIEM exports (alerts + audit streams) and a dedicated S3 bucket with CMK. Thoughts on RBAC for log access and KMS boundary? @mike @jenna

mike: Storage cost will bump. Can we do 90d hot + 275d cold (S3 Standard -> Glacier Deep Archive)? We already have lifecycle rules for /siem/ — will need rule update and cost estimate.

jenna: RBAC suggestion: create a security-log-reader role that only allows s3:GetObject on the siem bucket + CloudTrailRead for console access. No s3:ListBucket. Use short-lived STS sessions for humans. Example IAM snippet for review:
```
{
  "Effect": "Allow",
  "Action": ["s3:GetObject"],
  "Resource": ["arn:aws:s3:::redwood-siem/*"]
}
```

sara: Compliance note: 365d is reasonable for infra audit logs, but product telemetry may contain PII so we need a redaction step before exporting to SIEM. Also confirm EU data residency — EU customers' logs must land in eu- buckets.

alex: About KMS — do we go Redwood-managed CMK or customer-managed CMK (customer KMS)? Prefer customer-managed for rotation/audit. Any impact on SIEM ingestion or cross-account decrypt?

mike: Splunk/our SIEM supports SSE-KMS on S3. If we use a CMK, we must add the splunk-ingest-role to the key policy (or create a grant). Cross-account decrypt is the usual gotcha. Also expect slightly more GetObject/Decrypt calls and egress costs.

jenna: Also recommend a UI + backend change: hide "Download logs" in Console unless the principal is in security-log-reader. Enforce server-side ACLs and emit an audit event for every download. We can do middleware check + audit log.

alex: For incident response / vuln triage: implement a "break-glass" emergency-access role that requires 2FA + an incident ticket number and is time-limited. All access via break-glass should be fully audited and emailed to sec@redwood.

sara: Also: tag exported records with retention_policy and residency fields so forensics can filter quickly. I'll add the retention justification for legal.

sec-bot: WARNING: export-job-317 failed yesterday (ts: 1763720000) — error: AccessDenied on s3:GetObject. Suspected missing KMS cross-account permission for splunk-ingest-role.

mike: I'll open an infra ticket to update the KMS policy and grant decrypt to the ingest role. Will also produce an estimated monthly cost delta (~$1.2k) for moving to 365d.

alex: Can we get an RFC + PR with proposed IAM/Terraform by EOD Friday? I'll collate decisions and escalation path.

jenna: I'll add a migration plan: phase 1 (90d hot + 275d cold), monitor cost & query latency, then full 365d after 30 days if usage OK. Will include Terraform example and migration playbook.

sara: I'll draft the compliance checklist (PII redaction steps, retention justification, EU buckets, access review cadence) and drop it here.

alex: Thanks all — ping me if you need help. :thumbsup:
